chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
When the boy is able to endure fasting for three consecutive days, then fasting the month of Ramadan becomes obligatory upon him.
ai.seo_question: At what age or stage of development does fasting become obligatory for a boy in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi outlines the principle of gradual obligation (tadrij) in Shia jurisprudence, where a child's readiness is assessed through a trial period of three consecutive days rather than immediate full compliance. This threshold signifies the transition from mere encouragement to legal accountability (taklif), reflecting the scholarly view that fasting capacity is determined by physical endurance and mental maturity. It underscores the practical application of preparing the next generation for religious duties through manageable steps.
